sub: Named after aṭ-ṭalāq, divorce, the subject of its rulings
theme: How to end a marriage fairly when it must end: the right time, the waiting period, housing, support and nursing. Every ruling comes with a promise: whoever fears Allah, He makes a way out.
story: Revealed in Madinah, after the divorce rulings of Sūrat al-Baqarah. People began making mistakes in applying those rulings, so this surah came to correct them. It is also called the shorter Sūrat an-Nisāʾ.

It does not change the earlier rules. It teaches a careful way to divorce, so a marriage ends only after every chance to reconcile is gone. It also answers what was still open: the waiting period for women without periods or who are pregnant, and housing, support and nursing.

Reports link some ayat to events: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar divorcing his wife during her period (ayah 1), ʿAwf ibn Mālik’s captured son escaping (ayat 2–3), and a question about women the earlier rulings had not mentioned (ayah 4).

sections.title: Divorce with care, and a way out
sections.meaning: If divorce must happen, do it at the right time, keep count of the waiting period, and don’t put her out of her home. Near its end, keep her kindly or part kindly, with two witnesses. Whoever fears Allah, He gives a way out and unexpected provision.
points: Divorce at the right time and keep count of the waiting period
She stays in her home; perhaps Allah brings something new
Near the end: keep her kindly or part kindly, with two witnesses
Whoever fears Allah: a way out and unexpected provision
Rely on Allah and He is enough; everything has a measure
sections.matters: Divorce is often rushed in anger. This section slows it down: a set time, a waiting period in the same home, and a calm decision at the end. It also holds one of the Quran’s most hopeful promises, for any hardship.
sections.story: Reportedly ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar divorced his wife during her period. The Prophet ﷺ was angry, told him to take her back, and said any divorce should come in a clean period. Ayat 2–3 are also linked to ʿAwf ibn Mālik, whose son was captured.
explained: The Prophet ﷺ is addressed, but the ruling is for all believers. Divorce li-ʿiddatihinna: when the waiting period can start at once, in a clean period without intimacy, so her wait is not stretched. Count the days. She keeps her home unless she commits a clear wrong (either adultery or open abuse of his family). Perhaps his heart will change.

As the waiting period nears its end, decide calmly: keep her with kindness or let her go with kindness, never with insults or harm. Bring two just witnesses and testify honestly. Then the promise: whoever fears Allah gets a way out of every difficulty, provision from where he never expected, and Allah’s sufficiency when he relies on Him.
teaches: Even when a marriage ends, stay within Allah’s limits.
Don’t decide in anger; time may change hearts.
Part kindly, just as you would stay kindly.
Taqwā opens a way out of any hardship.
Trust Allah fully, while still using the means.
sections.hook: Ayah 1 says al-ʿiddah twice (li-ʿiddatihinna, aḥṣū al-ʿiddah). Ayah 2 ends with wa man yattaqi Allāh, and ayah 3 answers with wa man yatawakkal ʿalā Allāh.

sections.title: Waiting periods, housing and fair support
sections.meaning: Women whose periods have stopped, and those who have not had them, wait three months. A pregnant woman waits until she gives birth. Lodge divorced women as your means allow, without harming them. Support the pregnant until birth, pay a mother who nurses, and let each spend what he can.
points: No periods, or not yet: three months. Pregnant: until birth
This is Allah’s command; taqwā brings ease, forgiveness and reward
Lodge them as you can; don’t pressure them to leave
Support the pregnant, pay for nursing, and agree fairly
Spend by your means; after hardship, Allah brings ease
sections.matters: It fills the gaps Al-Baqarah left: every divorced woman now has a clear waiting period, and her housing and the child’s nursing are protected. It ends with hope for anyone short of money: Allah asks only what He gave, and ease is coming.
sections.story: Reportedly, after Al-Baqarah gave the waiting period, people said some women had not been mentioned: the young, the older whose periods had stopped, and the pregnant. Ayah 4 answered them.
explained: Al-Baqarah set three monthly cycles for most divorced women. This ayah covers the rest: women whose periods have stopped, and those who have not had periods, wait three months. A pregnant woman’s wait ends when she gives birth, whether divorced or widowed. Whoever fears Allah, He makes his affairs easy, forgives his sins, and enlarges his reward.

In the waiting period, house her where you live, as you can afford, and don’t make life hard to push her out. If she is pregnant, support her until the birth. If she then nurses the baby, pay her and agree kindly; if you can’t agree, another woman may nurse. Each spends by his means.
teaches: Never use housing or money to pressure someone out.
Separated parents should still agree kindly over the child.
Spend what you can; Allah asks no more than He gave.
sections.hook: Wa man yattaqi Allāh returns in ayah 4 and again in ayah 5, each time with a new reward. Page 559 starts at ayah 6: uskinūhunna, “lodge them”.

sections.title: Warning from ruined towns, then the light
sections.meaning: Many towns defied Allah and His messengers, were called to a hard account, and ended in loss, with worse prepared in the Hereafter. So people of understanding, fear Allah: He sent a Reminder and a Messenger to bring believers from darkness into light. He made seven heavens and earths like them.
points: Towns that defied Allah tasted the result: loss
A severe punishment ahead; so fear Allah, people of understanding
A Reminder and a Messenger: from darkness into light
Believe and do good: gardens forever, the best provision
Seven heavens, earths like them; His knowledge surrounds all
sections.matters: After the rulings comes the reason to keep them. Nations that ignored Allah’s commands were ruined. The Allah who sent these laws created the seven heavens and knows everything, so no wrong done in private escapes Him.
sections.story: Reportedly ayah 11 was about believers from the People of the Book. Otherwise no specific incident: the section warns anyone who would ignore the rulings above.
explained: How many towns rebelled against their Lord and His messengers! They were called to a severe account and punished terribly. They tasted the bitter result of their choices and ended in loss, and on top of that, a severe punishment waits for them in the Hereafter.

So fear Allah, you with sound minds and faith. He has sent down a Reminder and a Messenger ﷺ reciting clear ayat, to bring believers out of darkness into light, and into gardens forever. Allah created seven heavens and as many earths, and His command descends through them, so you know His power and knowledge cover everything.
teaches: Learn from nations that ignored Allah’s commands.
A sound mind leads to taqwā.
The Quran and the Prophet ﷺ lead from darkness to light.
Faith with good deeds brings gardens forever.
Nothing is outside Allah’s power or knowledge.
sections.hook: Fattaqū Allāh in ayah 10 echoes wattaqū Allāha rabbakum in ayah 1. The section runs from towns (qaryah, 8) to seven heavens and earths (12).

groups.text: If you divorce, do it at the right time and count the waiting period. She stays in her home; these are Allah’s limits.
Near its end, keep her or part kindly, with witnesses. Fear Allah: He gives a way out and provision. Rely on Him: He suffices.
Three months for women without periods; birth ends a pregnant woman’s wait. This is Allah’s command, and taqwā brings ease and reward.
House them as you can, don’t harm them, support the pregnant, pay for nursing, and settle matters kindly.
Each spends by his means. Allah asks only what He gave, and He brings ease after hardship.
Many towns defied Allah and His messengers; they were called to account, punished, and ended in loss.
So fear Allah, people of understanding. He sent a Reminder and a Messenger to bring believers from darkness into light.
Allah created seven heavens and earths like them, so you know His power and knowledge cover everything.

1.explain: Addressed to the Prophet ﷺ, meant for all. Divorce li-ʿiddatihinna: in a clean period without intimacy, so the wait isn’t prolonged. She stays home unless she commits a clear wrong, fāḥishah mubayyinah. Perhaps he regrets and takes her back.
1.why: Reportedly ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar divorced his wife during her period. The Prophet ﷺ was angry and told him to take her back, wait for a clean period, and then divorce, if he still wished, before any intimacy.

2.explain: Balaghna ajalahunna: nearly at the end of the wait. Decide calmly: keep her bi-maʿrūf, kindly, or let the wait end and part kindly, without insults. Two just witnesses prevent later disputes. Taqwā brings a makhraj, a way out.
2.why: Reportedly ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī came to the Prophet ﷺ: enemies had captured his son, and he was poor. He was told to fear Allah, be patient, and often say lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh. His son escaped.

3.explain: Provision from where he never imagined. Tawakkul: rely on Allah while still using the means, and He is ḥasbuh, enough. Allah’s will always comes to pass, but everything has a qadr: a set time and measure.
3.why: Part of the ʿAwf ibn Mālik report: his son came home driving the enemy’s animals. Another report: when “He is enough for him” came, some Companions said they would stop guarding their things; then “Allah will accomplish His purpose” came.

4.explain: Women whose periods have stopped, and those who have not had periods, wait three months. In irtabtum: if you are unsure, either of the ruling or of whether bleeding is a period. A pregnant woman’s wait ends at birth.
4.why: Reportedly, after Al-Baqarah gave the waiting period, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: “Some women are not mentioned: the young, the older whose periods have stopped, and the pregnant.” This ayah came. Other reports name a different questioner.

5.explain: Dhālika amr Allāh: these rules are Allah’s own command, sent down to you, so hold to them. Taqwā brings two more gifts here: sins wiped away and a reward made great, even for small deeds.

6.explain: Uskinūhunna: house her in part of your home, min wujdikum, as you can afford, without pressuring her to leave. Support her if pregnant until birth. Pay a mother who nurses; if you can’t agree, another woman may nurse the child.

7.explain: Dhū saʿah: the well-off spend from their plenty; the one with little spends from what Allah gave him. Allah asks no one beyond what He gave. Then good news: after ʿusr, hardship, Allah brings yusr, ease.

8.explain: Ka-ayyin: how many! Many towns defied their Lord’s command and His messengers. The hard reckoning and terrible punishment are either the Hereafter, told in the past tense because it is certain, or what struck them in this world.

9.explain: Wabāl: the heavy, bitter result of their deeds. They tasted it and regretted it when regret was useless. Their end was khusr: loss in this world and the next.

10.explain: On top of worldly ruin, a severe punishment waits. So fear Allah, ulul-albāb, people of sound minds who believe, and don’t be like them. Allah has sent you a dhikr, a Reminder: the Quran.

11.explain: He sent a Messenger ﷺ reciting clear ayat, to bring believers from the darkness of disbelief and ignorance into the light of faith and knowledge. Whoever believes and does good enters gardens forever, with the best provision.
11.why: Reportedly revealed about those among the People of the Book who believed.

12.explain: Allah created seven heavens and as many earths; how and where is left unexplained. His amr, both His law and His running of creation, descends among them, so you know His power and all-surrounding knowledge.
